# Selective Availability: Two Separate GPS Changes

Selective Availability deliberately degraded public GPS signals for national security. The US government stopped using the feature in May 2000, at President Bill Clinton’s direction, to make civil and commercial GPS more useful worldwide.

That operational change was distinct from a September 2007 announcement about the future GPS III generation. The government said GPS III would be procured without Selective Availability, specifying its omission from that generation rather than announcing a new switch in use. The procurement choice made the 2000 policy durable for GPS III.
